article_manifest.title: Mali: Dozo hunters and jihadists clash for a village near Djenné
article_manifest.original_title: Mali: chasseurs dozos et jihadistes s'affrontent pour un village près de Djenné
article_manifest.summary: In Mali, the village of Sounga, which belongs to the commune of Mougna, near Djenné in the Mopti region, continues to resist the jihadists of Jnim, linked to al-Qaeda While the surrounding villages have bowed to the domination of the jihadists, Sounga refuses to submit, provoking violent clashes last week between the Jnim jihadists and the traditional Dozo hunters, who are trying to protect the populations in this part of the territory where the Malian army is not present .

article_manifest.title: A strategic turning point
article_manifest.original_title: Un tournant stratégique
article_manifest.summary: L’approbation par le Parlement algérien du déploiement de troupes au Niger marque un tournant majeur dans les relations entre les deux pays. Au-delà de son caractère historique pour Alger, cette décision traduit une volonté de renforcer la coopération sécuritaire dans un Sahel confronté à la persistance des violences terroristes, à la criminalité transfrontalière.

article_manifest.title: Tillabéri: riders of tricycles and motorcycles adeydeyta announce a 48-hour strike
article_manifest.original_title: Tillabéri : les conducteurs de tricycles et de motos adeydeyta annoncent une grève de 48 heures
article_manifest.summary: In a notice dated 27 October 2026 and addressed to the managing director of the urban municipality, the Syndicat national des taxis tricycles du Niger (SNTTN), Tillabéri section, announces a work stoppage from Sunday 1 to Monday 2 November 2026. Through this walkout, they intend to protest against the measures restricting traffic in certain areas, taken by the authorities for safety reasons .

article_manifest.title: Bamako: three murder cases solved by the police
article_manifest.original_title: Bamako : trois affaires de meurtres élucidées par la police
article_manifest.summary: Bamako, October 28 (AMAP) The National Police has clarified three cases of murders and assassinations that occurred recently in Bamako, with the arrest of several suspects within 24 to 48 hours. The Director General of the National Police, Comptroller General Youssouf Koné, presented the results of the investigations on Wednesday at a press briefing held at the Directorate General of the National Police (DGPN), noted AMAP .

article_manifest.title: Mali: Turkish drones and Russian command, the responsibilities behind the deadly strikes

Scheduled over two days, the work was opened by the Comrade Secretary General of the MGDP, Intendant Colonel-Major Yamba Léonard OUOBA .

article_manifest.title: Sensitive areas, oil sites: the deployment of Algerian troops in Niger is becoming clearer

article_manifest.summary: If the decision to send soldiers to Niger looks, for Algiers, like a confirmation of the support given to the Niamey regime, the operation also aims to secure Algerian economic interests south of the border Following the vote, on 25 October, of the two chambers of Parliament authorizing an intervention by the Algerian army in Niger, President Abdelmadjid Tebboune announced the dispatch of military units in order to "protect Algeria's energy interests" and to implement the provisions of the military and security cooperation agreement signed on 21 October with Niamey .

article_manifest.summary: In Mali, four pro-democracy activists detained by state security for nearly six months in unknown locations and outside any judicial framework reappeared on Tuesday, October 20. On the other hand, there is still no news of the lawyer and former minister Mountaga Tall, who was the first to be kidnapped by state security last May.

article_manifest.title: Bamako: one dead and several injured in an accident on the Koulouba-Kati axis
article_manifest.original_title: Bamako : un mort et plusieurs blessés dans un accident sur l’axe Koulouba-Kati
article_manifest.summary: A serious traffic accident occurred on Tuesday 27 October on the Koulouba-Kati axis, at the turn of Point G, near the GSSP camp. article_manifest.original_title: Mali : les FAMa frappent deux positions terroristes dans les secteurs de Talhandak et Ménaka
article_manifest.summary: Mali: the FAMa strike two terrorist positions in the Talhandak and Menaka sectors The Malian Armed Forces (FAMa) announce two targeted strikes carried out on 20 and 21 October 2026 in the Talhandak and Menaka sectors. According to the General Staff of the Armed Forces, these operations made it possible to neutralize a position of regroupment of individuals presented as terrorists and to destroy a vehicle assigned to them .

article_manifest.title: Press/West Africa: strike in Senegal, price drop in Mali and major economic projects
article_manifest.original_title: Presse/Afrique de l’Ouest : grève au Sénégal, baisse des prix au Mali et grands projets économiques
article_manifest.summary: The continuation of the general strike in Senegal, the announced fall in meat prices in Mali and investment projects in Ghana are among the topics that are attracting the attention of the West African press on Thursday. In Burkina Faso, the dialogue with Türkiye focuses in particular on security and investments, while Benin opens its budget session on several legislative and social priorities In Senegal, the Front syndical pour la défense du travail (FSDT) claims a success rate of 90% for the first day of its general strike organized Wednesday, October 21, Pressafrik reports.

article_manifest.title: Portrait Article reserved for our subscribers Chérif Ould Taher, the sulphurous Malian intermediary behind the last hostage releases in the Sahel Kidnapped in 2025 by the Islamic State in the Sahel, a Swiss woman and an Austrian woman were released on Wednesday. As for an American, in August, this businessman, considered one of the main drug traffickers in northern Mali, played a key role.
article_manifest.original_title: Portrait Article réservé à nos abonnés Chérif Ould Taher, le sulfureux intermédiaire malien derrière les dernières libérations d’otages au Sahel Enlevées en 2025 par l’Etat islamique au Sahel, une Suissesse et une Autrichienne ont été libérées mercredi. Comme pour un Américain, en août, cet homme d’affaires, considéré comme l’un des principaux narcotrafiquants dans le nord du Mali, a joué un rôle clé.
article_manifest.summary: They had been abducted three months apart in Agadez, in northern Niger, where they had lived for many years. The Austrian Eva Gretzmacher, 74, and the Swiss Claudia Abbt, 68, respectively kidnapped in January and April 2025 by the Islamic State in the Sahel (ISIS), were released Wednesday, October 21 . Presumably held in the sanctuary of the jihadist group, in the Menaka region of neighboring Mali, they were recovered in southern Libya by a unit of the Libyan National Army of Marshal Khalifa Haftar and taken by plane to Benghazi, the stronghold of the strongman of eastern Libya .

article_manifest.title: Mali: Army, Russia’s ‘Africa Corps’ Commit New Abuses
article_manifest.original_title: Mali: Army, Russia’s ‘Africa Corps’ Commit New Abuses
article_manifest.summary: (Nairobi) – Mali’s armed forces and the allied Russia-controlled Africa Corps have committed new atrocities against civilians in central Mali during renewed fighting, Human Rights Watch said today. On September 16, 2026, an apparent military drone strike in Guélédié village, Mopti region, killed eight civilians and injured at least six others. Between May and August, Malian and Africa Corps forces held numerous detainees inhumanely in a metal container at an army base in Sévaré town, Mopti region, where many were tortured, including with severe beatings, electric shock, and waterboarding.

article_manifest.title: Burkina Faso Restores Death Penalty
article_manifest.original_title: Burkina Faso Restores Death Penalty
article_manifest.summary: Burkina Faso’s unelected parliament has unanimously adopted a new penal code that restores the death penalty for high treason, terrorism, acts of espionage, parricide and importation of expired or prohibited products. The country had abolished the death penalty for ordinary crimes in 2018 while its last known judicial execution took place in 1988. Reinstating capital punishment sends a chilling message to critics of the military junta and risks becoming another tool to suppress dissent.

article_manifest.title: Bamako Grand Market: Two suspects...
article_manifest.original_title: Grand marché de Bamako : Deux suspects...
article_manifest.summary: Great Market of Bamako: Two suspects arrested, 290 million CFA francs in damage and a trailer truck seized! By patiently following up the trail of several burglaries committed between 2023 and 2026, Chief Commissioner Josué KAMATÉ and his investigators from the Police Station of the Shopping Centre managed to identify two suspects. Eighteen shops were reportedly targeted, including fourteen at the Bamako Grand Market .

article_manifest.title: Mali: the FAMa hit a group of motorcyclists in the forest of Ouagadou
article_manifest.original_title: Mali : les FAMa frappent un groupe de motocyclistes dans la forêt de Ouagadou
article_manifest.summary: The Malian Armed Forces (FAMa) announce that they carried out a targeted strike on Tuesday, October 20, 2026, against a group of more than a dozen motorcyclists spotted in the forest of Ouagadou, near the village of Ngoma Koura According to the General Staff of the Armed Forces, several terrorist elements were neutralized during this operation carried out as part of Operation Dougoukoloko.

article_manifest.title: Decryption Article reserved for our subscribers The war between the Islamic State and Al-Qaida is gaining momentum in the Sahel In the territorial and ideological conflict between the two Sahelian jihadist organizations since 2019 in this border area, straddling Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger, the bloody episode of October 9 could be the deadliest.
article_manifest.original_title: Décryptage Article réservé à nos abonnés La guerre entre l’Etat islamique et Al-Qaida prend de l’ampleur au Sahel Dans le conflit territorial et idéologique qui oppose les deux organisations djihadistes sahéliennes depuis 2019 dans cette zone frontalière, à cheval sur le Mali, le Burkina Faso et le Niger, l’épisode sanglant du 9 octobre pourrait être le plus meurtrier.
article_manifest.summary: For the second time in just over a month, the jihadists of the Islamic State in the Sahel (ISIS) and those of the Group for the Support of Islam and Muslims (GSIM), Al-Qaida's regional franchise, fought a pitched battle in the desert north of Burkina Faso. On October 9, in the vicinity of the village of Ganadaouri, hundreds of their fighters clashed . The first would have won, claiming to have neutralized 400 men of the GSIM and seized 100 of their motorcycles as well as hundreds of weapons.

article_manifest.title: Burkina Faso's junta reinstates the death penalty The military regime had officially announced its intention to reinstate the death penalty by passing a bill last December. It had been abolished in 2018.
article_manifest.original_title: La junte du Burkina Faso rétablit la peine de mort Le régime militaire avait annoncé officiellement son intention de rétablir la peine de mort en adoptant un projet de loi en décembre dernier. Elle avait été abolie en 2018.
article_manifest.summary: Burkina Faso reintroduced the death penalty into a new penal code on Tuesday, October 20, after a unanimous vote of the unelected members of the People's Legislative Assembly (PLA), which serves as the parliament in the junta-run country. At the head of the military regime that came to power at the end of September 2022 by a coup d 'état, Captain Ibrahim Traoré governs the country with an iron fist Dozens of critical voices, as well as journalists and magistrates have been kidnapped and sometimes forcibly conscripted to fight the jihadists who are undermining the country, according to international NGOs.

article_manifest.title: In Mali, more than 40 civilians killed by armed men in the Ménaka region, according to local sources. These bloody attacks targeted camps belonging mainly to the Daoussahak community, from which the armed group Mouvement pour le salut de l 'Azawad, close to the ruling junta in Bamako, came, according to sources interviewed by Agence France-Presse.
article_manifest.original_title: Au Mali, plus de 40 civils tués par des hommes armés dans la région de Ménaka, selon des sources locales Ces attaques sanglantes ont visé des campements appartenant majoritairement à la communauté des Daoussahak, dont est issu le groupe armé Mouvement pour le salut de l’Azawad, proche de la junte au pouvoir à Bamako, d’après des sources interrogées par l’Agence France-Presse.
article_manifest.summary: More than forty civilians were killed on Sunday, October 18, during attacks perpetrated by armed men in the Ménaka region, in northeastern Mali, causing population displacement, several security sources, local and associative, reported Monday to Agence France-Presse (AFP) These bloody attacks, carried out by armed men who arrived on motorcycles, targeted, according to these sources, camps belonging mainly to the Daoussahak community, from which the armed group Mouvement pour le salut de l 'Azawad (MSA), close to the ruling junta in Bamako, came.

article_manifest.title: Ménaka and Douentza regions: Successful FAMa precision strikes against terrorists As part of Operation Dougoukoloko, the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa), supported by their partners, successfully carried out a series of targeted strikes on 17 and 18 October 2026 in the Ménaka and Douentza sectors, neutralizing important terrorist bases and gatherings.
article_manifest.original_title: Régions de Ménaka et Douentza : Succès des frappes de précision des FAMa contre les terroristes Dans le cadre de l'opération Dougoukoloko, les Forces armées maliennes (FAMa), appuyées par leurs partenaires, ont mené avec succès une série de frappes ciblées les 17 et 18 octobre 2026 dans les secteurs de Ménaka et Douentza, neutralisant d'importantes bases et rassemblements terroristes..
article_manifest.summary: The information was made public Monday, October 19, 2026 by the General Staff of the Armed Forces through a press release, which indicates that the FAMa continue their permanent operations of surveillance, control and security of the national territory According to the security source, on Saturday, October 17, 2026, the exploitation of precise intelligence made it possible to locate, 65 km southwest of the city of Menaka, a large base housing several terrorist elements as well as war and logistics equipment.

article_manifest.title: Menaka and Douentza: FAMa strike a terrorist base and concentration point
article_manifest.original_title: Ménaka et Douentza : les FAMa frappent une base et un point de concentration terroristes
article_manifest.summary: Menaka and Douentza: the FAMa strike a terrorist base and concentration point In a communiqué dated 19 October 2026, the General Staff of the Armed Forces announced two precision strikes carried out on 17 and 18 October, south-west of Menaka and then Douentza, as part of Operation Dougoukoloko. Surveillance, control and security operations of the national territory continue The General Staff of the Armed Forces informed the opinion that the Malian Armed Forces, supported by their partners, carried out two new strikes as part of Operation Dougoukoloko.

article_manifest.original_title: Opération Dougoukoloko : Les FAMa frappent deux positions terroristes à Dioura et dans la région ...
article_manifest.summary: Operation Dougoukoloko: The FAMa strike two terrorist positions in Dioura and in the Ségou region As part of Operation Dougoukoloko, the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa), supported by their partners, targeted two terrorist positions on 14 and 15 October 2026 According to the General Staff of the Armed Forces, a base located northwest of Dioura and a regroupment point spotted in the Ségou region were hit following information deemed accurate.
